newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Asian Metal-S.Korea market dampened by defaults.
newsitem.headline: Asian Metal-S.Korea market dampened by defaults.

text.p: A default on debt repayments by an unlisted South Korean wire maker has clouded the domestic copper market, battered by a series of corporate collapses, traders in Seoul said on Thursday.
The default also dampened domestic copper demand and continued to force local copper buyers, especially cable makers, to ship their stock overseas to cut carrying costs, they said.
Donghyeong Magnet Wire Co Ltd defaulted on debt repayments of about 50 billion to 60 billion won early this week, a company official said.
The official said the company's main creditor was the Korea First Bank, which has also been suffering from Hanbo Steel and Sammi Steel's defaults on debt payments.
Traders said the company has bought more than 800 tonnes of copper rods a month from domestic copper rod makers for its factory.
"Suppliers are offering copper at premiums of $50-$60 a tonne CIF Pusan over the LME cash prices. But no one appeared to be buying copper at the moment," a trader with a major trading house said.
"We have not seen this kind of slowdown in the domestic market. It's really bad," the trader said.
The domestic aluminium market was also suffering with more defaults by small and medium-sized metal companies expected, traders said.
However, the domestic aluminium market continued to experience a slight shortage since most traders have reduced their inventories in the second quarter due to heavy carrying costs, traders said.
Aluminium import premiums for spot delivery were unchanged at $95-$100 a tonne CIF Pusan over LME's cash prices, traders said.
Domestic aluminium prices remained firm at 1,550,000-1,560,000 won a tonne due to unusual supply tightness in the domestic market over the past week, they said.
Domestic copper and zinc prices were flat at 2,467,000 won and 1,348,000 won a tonne respectively over the past week.
